correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), Fourier characters of Z/n x Z/2 diagonalize the prism Hamiltonian. Averaging the squared propagator gives \(\mu_{a,b}=N_{a,b}/(2n)\), where N is the exact count of equal-energy ordered character pairs with difference (a,b). Equal-layer counts are the solutions of \(2k\equiv a\pmod n\). For unequal layers, the equality \(x_k-x_l=2\) is exhausted using that \(x_k-1\) is an algebraic integer whose conjugates lie in \([-1,1]\); the Kronecker lemma is proved from integral norms and bounded power polynomials. Thus the only cosine-eigenvalue pairs are (0,-2),(1,-1),(2,0), giving contributions exclusively at \(4\mid n\) and \(6\mid n\). The displayed indexed eigenvalues sum to 1 in the trivial character and have the correct 2n count, and their positivity proves the rank formula for all orders. Independent projector calculations (3<=\(n\le24\)) and ordered-pair counts (3<=\(n\le18\)) corroborate but do not replace this infinite proof.

value.rationale: The prism \(C_n\square K_2\) is a canonical regular two-ring quantum transport graph. The theorem classifies a natural infinite family, gives every eigenvalue and all null directions, and isolates a sharp and nonobvious arithmetic resonance at divisibility by four and six (for example rank 11 of 24 at \(n=12\)). The cyclotomic-integer rigidity method is a structural reason no other cross-layer resonances occur, rather than a numerical or routine special-case enumeration. A precise spectral rank invariant is useful for diagnosing long-time transport memory and symmetry.
